Just in the last month we saw Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, Gemini 3.6 Flash, and Kimi K3, and keeping track of which one is best (and cheapest) for planning versus implementation is now a task on its own. Auto Model is Kilo Code’s answer to that: you pick a tier (frontier, balanced, efficient, or free) and the router selects the underlying model per request. tweets.text: We tested our Auto Model router against picking models manually. Same backend task, three setups: 1. Kilo Auto Model (auto frontier for planning + auto efficient for building) 2. Claude Sonnet 5 for everything 3. GPT 5.6 for everything Result: all three shipped functionally identical services, 29/30 logic checks passed. But Auto Model did it for $1.26 vs $2.90 (Sol) and $2.47 (Sonnet), and was the only one that matched the API contract exactly.

They're *only* against Paramount suddenly...what's different here?🤔 DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) Benedict Cumberbatch, Benedict Wong & Alan Cumming have written an op-ed together, asking for the UK Government to block the Warner Bros/Paramount merger. “A TV and cinema calamity could be disastrous for what you watch and what you know. Act now to stop that.” 🔗: theguardian.com/commentis
